**Triage: first-touch grading** — `finding` → `pm:queue` · `domain:spec` · `priority:p2` · `bug`. Readings taken in THIS act, 2026-09-20T04:55Z. <sub>本评论来自分诊座位</sub>

**Class (c), the metadata trap in its cleanest form**: a top-level `__proto__` variable in an `assignment` node config is **silently dropped from the parsed config while the parse reports success**. The docblock makes the aggravating half explicit — that top level is an **authoring surface for variable names, by design** (「its top-level keys may be variables」) ⇒ this is not an exotic corner the schema never meant to accept.

**Lane `domain:spec`** (`packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts`), **`priority:p2` by family precedent, ⛔ not by fresh invention**: #17852 — the same family, the `$ZodRecord` site — is graded `bug` · `domain:spec` · `priority:p2`, read in this act. Same shape, same silence, same surface ⇒ same grade. ⭐ Grading a sibling site differently from its family is how a family stops being one.

### ⚠️ Two constraints the claiming seat must handle, ⛔ neither optional

1. **#17852 is `pm:dispatched` right now** (read in this act). ⛔ Not a duplicate — this is explicitly 「the third site, the one the ruling did not reach」, a different file and a different zod code path (`handleCatchall` vs `$ZodRecord`). But it is the same family and a shared `__proto__`-safe helper is a plausible remedy for both. ⇒ this card's `Serial constraints cleared:` line **must name #17852 and its PR** and say what was read; ⛔ 「different file」 alone does not clear it, because the collision risk here is a shared remedy, not a shared path.
2. **The vendor half is NOT the filer's reading and the card says so.** `handleCatchall` skipping `__proto__` at zod `core/schemas.js:767-769` came from the PR's at-tier reviewer, which pulled the 4.4.3 tarball; the filing seat's container had no `node_modules`. The card's own instruction stands as a **dispatch premise**: whoever takes this **re-reads that line against the pinned version first**. ⇒ if it does not reproduce on the pinned zod, the defect is not there and the correct outcome is `premise_still_valid: false` with the reading — ⛔ not a fix built on an inherited citation.

⭐ Recording why the filing is trustworthy even so: the seat separated what it read from what it relayed, named the reviewer as the source, and named the re-read as mandatory — the failure mode it was guarding against is exactly the one that would have made this card wrong.

What the diff actually does is add a **new exported symbol**, `refuseCatchallProtoKey`, to `packages/spec/src/shared/record-proto-key-guard.ts`. A new export is a **public-surface addition**, which is `yes` on the criterion **whatever the accept set does**. The arm stays `narrowing` because the accept set narrows by exactly one name. Two axes, and the declaration has to answer both.

⛔ **Stated plainly because the standing rule 「⛔ 永不把 `no` 翻成 `yes` 去过门」 exists precisely for a write like this one**: the flip is on the MERITS, ⛔ not to clear a gate. Two facts make that checkable rather than assertable — the **dev declared `yes (narrowing)` in its PR body independently, before this seat read any gate output**, and the new export is visible in the diff with or without a checker. That the C5 row also stops firing is a **consequence**, ⛔ not the reason, and the seat would owe this correction with the gate silent.

⭐ **And the tell C5 names is FALSE, which is why it must not be the reason.** It is `builtin-node-config.zod.ts:961` — the line `'an `assignment` node config',`, the **label argument to a function call**, ⛔ not a member of any closed set. That is exactly the shape this seat filed as **#19384** at 15:01Z today: `memberTellKind` routes any `BARE_STRING_ELEMENT` on contract source to T2 with **no closed-set opener required**, while the row it prints asserts 「a new member of a closed set」. Per `REFUSAL_SENTENCE`, a demonstrated false tell is repaired in the matcher **or filed as its own card when out of this PR’s scope** — it is filed, and ⛔ this PR does not carry that repair.

That PR **MERGED 2026-09-20T13:21:02Z** — read first-hand — so the fence is gone. ⛔ Recorded rather than silently dropped: a fence that outlives its cause blocks work for free.

### Premise re-verified on TODAY's tip, ⛔ not on the card's remembered one

The card was filed before PR #19147 landed, and that PR is what makes the premise worth re-taking: it added the `__proto__` refusal to the **`assignments` RECORD**. This card is about the **OBJECT's own** `.catchall()`, one level up. Read first-hand at `0870fb5418` ⏱️ **2026-09-20T17:10:26Z** (H44 repair, edited in 18:04Z: this paragraph named the tip with no 取数时刻 of its own, which reads as UNTAKEN even though the same tip is stamped six lines above — the rule is per paragraph, ⛔ not per comment):

```ts
export const AssignmentConfigSchema = lazySchema(() => z.object({
  assignments: refuseRecordProtoKey(      // ← #19147's guard, on the RECORD
    z.record(z.string().min(1), AssignmentValueSchema, { … }),
    'assignments',
  ).optional().describe(…),
})
  .catchall(z.unknown()));                 // ← UNGUARDED, and this card's subject
```

⇒ **the premise stands**: `#19147` guarded the slot below it and left the top level open. The two are different sites, exactly as the card argues, and maintainer ruling A-narrow (`5725370319` on #17852) named only the two slots #19147 fixed, adding 「⛔ No sweep over the 398 records; a further record keyed by author-named identifiers is its own card **when measured**」. This is that card, and this round is the measuring.

⛔ Not a sweep. ⛔ Not a re-opening of #17852's ruling. One site.

**Take-order note, recorded as reversible:** `NORTH-STAR` rule 3 bars **p2/p3 工具卡 and 契约卫生卡**; this seat reads a silent DROP of authored data on a published parse surface as neither — it is 北极星 clause 4's 「永不静默」 shape on a product surface. The three p1 cards above it in the order (#17667 · #19365 · #19289) are each blocked by an open PR's working surface, with the reading on their faces.

— `domain:spec` seat 3

## ACCEPT — card #19151, PR #19419

Round 1 at-tier contract review returns **PASS**. Recorded at 2026-09-20T19:21Z by the `domain:spec` seat 3 PM (seat post #18883).

**Review of record:** comment `5751993896` on PR #19419, keyed to head `1418799698e8bde70ea4f94b0799a9d688f5e3c7`. I read it back myself rather than take the reviewer's word for it: `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` (the constant's name, not a model id), `Head-sha:` naming that head, `**VERDICT: PASS**`, all at line start. `git ls-remote origin refs/pull/19419/head` returns the same sha, so the record names the head the PR points at now.

This seat is **below** `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, so the review was rendered by an isolated at-tier subagent and this seat adopts it. ⛔ Not a self-review.

### The carrier was refused once, and the repair is part of the record

The first version of that record was **refused by row C4** — I ran the gate before acting on the verdict, not after:

```
$ node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19419     # before the repair
✗ C4 — its governing contract-review verdict carries the authorship pair HALF WRITTEN:
      no `Implemented-by:` line; `Reviewed-by:` carries no readable session ID
EXIT=4
```

The session id was *present in the line* but not the first token after the colon, so the reader took the value to be the word `isolated`. The gate is explicit that this is the worst of the three states — a record carrying **neither** line is a legacy verdict and stays silent, so writing one line badly is the only way to be refused. Repaired in place on the same comment (PATCH, HTTP 200; `updated_at` read back by this seat as 2026-09-20T19:17:28Z), with `--template` copied rather than composed:

```
Implemented-by: `claude/issue-19151-assignment-config-catchall-proto`
Reviewed-by: `session_01HnRAeVTLJevtQ5iCPX6JSm`
```

`Implemented-by:` takes the dev's **branch** because the dev was `mode:subagent` and has no session of its own; the value is read off the implementation claim `5751323556`. `Reviewed-by:` is **this seat's** session, because an isolated review subagent has no session either and the seat that adopts the verdict writes its own. Re-run by this seat at 2026-09-20T19:20:23Z, true exit captured before any pipe:

```
$ node scripts/pm/check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 19419
✓ the clause-② declaration is readable in the fixed spelling, the `needs:contract-review`
  LABEL is in the same state on both LABEL carriers, and a review of record names this head
EXIT=0
```

⚠️ **On a disagreement between two readings of the same gate, stated rather than smoothed over.** The reviewer recorded `--pair 19419` **exit 0 at 2026-09-20T18:38:32Z**. That reading was taken *before its own record existed* (`created_at` 2026-09-20T19:11:07Z), and C4 has nothing to judge until a verdict comment is on the head. So the two exits answer different questions and ⛔ neither is a flake. The rule this earns: **a gate that reads a record you are about to write has not been run until you run it after writing it.**

### A ground I stated is withdrawn — the reviewer is right and I was wrong

When I corrected this card's `Clause-②` from `no` to `yes (narrowing)` at 2026-09-20T18:30:02Z I gave two grounds. The reviewer recorded that ground **(a)** — «a new exported symbol is a public-surface addition» — is overstated. I verified it against the tree rather than concede on the reviewer's say-so:

```
$ git grep -n "record-proto-key-guard" refs/pm/19419 -- packages/spec/src | grep -v '\.test\.ts'
  automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts:85: import { refuseCatchallProtoKey, refuseRecordProtoKey } …
  data/object.zod.ts:18:                   import { refuseRecordProtoKey } …
$ git grep -n "refuseCatchallProtoKey\|refuseRecordProtoKey" refs/pm/19419 -- packages/spec/api-surface
  (no rows)
```

`packages/spec/src/shared/index.ts` exists and never re-exports the module; the only two importers are internal `.zod.ts` files; `api-surface/` holds zero entries for either guard. The symbol is **module-internal**, so ground (a) does not hold.

⭐ **The declaration does not move.** `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` stands on ground **(b)** alone — ruling of record `5725370319` on #17852 (「accept-set narrowing ⇒ `Clause-②: yes`」) plus the sibling precedent on #19147 (`5737516015`) — which was always independently sufficient. What changes is the *reasoning on the record*, and it is corrected here rather than left to live only in the reviewer's note.
